newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan expects record 1997 oil activity.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan expects record 1997 oil activity.

text.p: The government of Saskatchewan, Canada's second biggest oil-producing province, said on Wednesday that six-month figures suggested it was set for a record year in energy industry activity.
Saskatchewan's energy and mines ministry said the number of licences issued for oil and gas wells by the end of June were up 50 and 54 percent respectively over the same period last year.
The activity was leading to high production levels with successful wells up by nearly 70 percent, the province said.

A total of 1,411 wells, including 1,035 oil wells, were drilled in the first half of this year. In the same period in 1996, the industry drilled 915 wells, including 624 oil wells, Saskatchewan's New Democratic Party government said.

"Last year was the fourth consecutive record-setting year for oil production and we believe we'll break that record again, assuming that prices hold," Energy and Mines Minister Eldon Lautermilch said in a statement.
Lautermilch said drilling rigs in the province were at full utilization levels and companies in oil producing regions were hiring every worker they could find.
"Basically, the oil sector is running at full capacity," he said.

World oil prices are lower than what the province had forecast in its most recent budget, so the government was not expecting a windfall in resource revenues, it said. Saskatchewan's royalties are commodity price-sensitive.
But high cash reserves from last year's strong crude prices were enabling companies to re-invest in aggressive drilling programs, the government said.
The highest activity levels this year were reported in the Estevan area in southeast Saskatchewan, followed by Lloydminster in the northwest.
The Kindersley area, known for its heavy oil activity, posted the strongest year-over-year jump in drilling activity, up 96 percent.

The top five drillers across Saskatchewan in the first half of 1997 were Renaissance Energy Ltd, Wascana Energy Inc, Stampeder Exploration Ltd, Husky Oil Operations Ltd and Talisman Energy Inc. Wascana is now a unit of Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
